why: Telemetry for the upstream-schema-change case, and the corpus's first case in which the loudest series belongs to the victim rather than to the answer. Every reading the text supports is small: the feed changed one field and one more appeared, so the change at the cause is a single unit, and the error at the reader is a share of orders. The two are deliberately not the same size, because they are not the same quantity -- a magnitude method ranks settlement first and the answer second, deterministically, and the case exists to penalise that. Both series are counted rather than sampled (a share of orders and a field count), so neither carries the corpus's plus-or-minus-two-per-cent jitter: a jittered field count would be a claim that a response sometimes had one and a half fields. There is deliberately no third series: a control showing settlement's other dependencies healthy would be a reading the incident text does not state, and a corpus that invents a quiet series to make its own argument is the shape every other rule here refuses.

series.why: the checkpoint `cp-mismatch` holds the symptom: the share of orders whose total disagreed, which the text states as a size ("a few cents") rather than as a share -- the share is the reading that makes the size locatable, and the baseline is zero because the text says totals matched again once the feed reverted

series.quote: carry a single rate field and now carries rate plus inverse
series.why: the checkpoint `cp-field-count` holds the change itself: one field before, two after, which is the whole of what moved on the answer and is a single unit of a count -- a magnitude method has nothing to be impressed by here, and the case is built so that this is the honest reading rather than a weakness of it

logs.body: WARN currency-rate parser: response carries rate and inverse; reading rate as before, which the feed rounds to two places
logs.quote: Settlement's parser still reads the old field, which is now rounded
logs.why: the checkpoint `cp-parser-log` holds this line: a reconstruction of what the parser would emit, since the incident text states the fact and not the message -- it is the only reading on the settlement side that names the field rather than the size of the error
